sections.heading: Section 1: Simple Linear Regression and Residuals

questions.q: In simple linear regression $\hat{y} = 3.5x + 12$, what is the residual $e_i = y_i - \hat{y}_i$ for an observation at $(x_i, y_i) = (4, 30)$?
What is the mathematical condition guaranteed by the OLS fit regarding the sum of all residuals $\sum_{i=1}^n e_i$?
questions.answer: The first normal equation $\frac{\partial \text{SSE}}{\partial \beta_0} = -2\sum (y_i - \beta_0 - \beta_1 x_i) = 0$ guarantees $\sum e_i = 0$.

questions.q: Given $\bar{x} = 10, \bar{y} = 25$, and fitted slope $\hat{\beta}_1 = 2$, compute the $y$-intercept $\hat{\beta}_0$.
questions.answer: Regression line passes through the centroid: $\hat{\beta}_0 = \bar{y} - \hat{\beta}_1 \bar{x} = 25 - 2(10) = 5$.

sections.heading: Section 3: Matrix Normal Equations and Projections

questions.q: State the matrix Normal Equations for the OLS weight vector $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ given design matrix $\mathbf{X}$ and target $\mathbf{y}$.
When is the Gram matrix $(\mathbf{X}^T \mathbf{X})$ strictly invertible?
choices: When the columns of $\mathbf{X}$ are linearly independent (full column rank)
When all elements in $\mathbf{X}$ are positive
When the target $\mathbf{y}$ has zero mean
questions.answer: Full column rank ensures $\mathbf{X}^T\mathbf{X}$ is positive definite and thus invertible.

questions.q: What geometric role does the hat matrix $\mathbf{H} = \mathbf{X}(\mathbf{X}^T \mathbf{X})^{-1} \mathbf{X}^T$ play?
choices: It orthogonal-projects target $\mathbf{y}$ onto the column space of $\mathbf{X}$ ($\,\hat{\mathbf{y}} = \mathbf{H}\mathbf{y}\,)$
It normalizes features to zero mean
questions.answer: $\mathbf{H}$ satisfies $\mathbf{H}^2 = \mathbf{H}$ (idempotent) and $\mathbf{H}^T = \mathbf{H}$ (symmetric), the definition of orthogonal projection.

sections.heading: Section 4: Goodness of Fit and Regularization

questions.q: In an evaluation, $\text{SSE} = 25$ and $\text{SST} = 100$. Compute the coefficient of determination $R^2$.
How does Ridge regression ($L_2$ penalty) resolve multicollinearity when $\mathbf{X}^T\mathbf{X}$ is ill-conditioned?
choices: It drops half the features automatically
It sets all correlated weights to zero
questions.answer: Adding $\lambda > 0$ along the diagonal shifts all eigenvalues up by $\lambda$, making the matrix well-conditioned.
